title: 谘商会冲上103：密歇根却走弱，美联储会因此改利率路径吗？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: There might be some election things in here, maybe some more optimism, but I wonder what you make of a higher consumer confidence because it's morning.
segments.zh: 这里面可能有一些选举因素，也许更乐观一些，但我想知道你怎么看消费者信心上升，因为现在是早上。

segments.en: It pushes back on the University of Michigan, which saw the current conditions weakening.
segments.zh: 这与密歇根大学的数据相矛盾，该数据显示当前状况正在减弱。

segments.en: Yes, you're right. We're going to see that standard justification of Dems getting excited, Republicans getting worried, but that hasn't hit the data yet.
segments.zh: 是的，你说得对。我们会看到标准的解释，即民主党人兴奋，共和党人担忧，但这还没有体现在数据中。

segments.en: That'll be next month. This is obviously a positive going into the holiday season, but again, you can't trade on this.
segments.zh: 那将是下个月。这显然是进入假日季节的积极因素，但同样，你不能据此进行交易。

segments.en: It's lovely that people are feeling better. Look, gas prices are coming down.
segments.zh: 人们感觉更好是好事。看，汽油价格正在下降。

segments.en: That's a big part of this. We obviously saw that in inflation expectations last week in the U-Mish, and this is probably echoing in that as well.
segments.zh: 这是很大一部分原因。我们上周在密歇根大学的通胀预期中明显看到了这一点，这可能也在其中有所反映。

segments.en: Do you think this would meaningfully change the Fed's rate path hike?
segments.zh: 你认为这会实质性改变美联储的利率路径吗？

segments.en: I know it's just one reading, but then it's just a fear consumer-based is confident.
segments.zh: 我知道这只是一个读数，但然后只是担心消费者信心十足。

segments.en: They will likely spend more and sugar more inflation and all of that.
segments.zh: 他们可能会花更多钱，加剧通胀等等。

segments.en: Yeah, I know. I heard you're saying, I think to your point, this doesn't materially necessarily hit their models in some way where aggregate demand would pick up.
segments.zh: 是的，我知道。我听到你说的了，我想针对你的观点，这不一定会在某种程度上实质性影响他们的模型，即总需求会回升。

segments.en: What I am excited about is what I didn't hear from Williams yesterday and what we're not really talking about yet, is that gas prices at the pump have fallen notably.
segments.zh: 我兴奋的是昨天没从威廉姆斯那里听到的，以及我们还没真正讨论的，是加油站油价明显下降了。

segments.en: This was being a big drag obviously now on core inflation moving forward.
segments.zh: 这显然曾是核心通胀的一个大拖累，现在情况在变化。

segments.en: We're going to get the reverse of what we've seen. Also financial conditions tightened quite nicely last week with the soft and equities.
segments.zh: 我们将看到与之前相反的情况。上周金融条件也随着软数据和权益资产而明显收紧。

segments.en: Williams came out yesterday speaking about some of these things he's seeing in residential sort of prices and other things, not being no wage-spire inflation and all that.
segments.zh: 威廉姆斯昨天谈到了他在地产市场等方面看到的一些情况，并不是工资螺旋式通胀之类的。

segments.en: That was great. Not yet seeing sort of this stickier inflation worry and it's still like headline-driven shocks.
segments.zh: 那很好。还没看到这种粘性通胀的担忧，仍然像是整体数据驱动的冲击。
